commands.name: approval-gate
commands.summary: Bind a relayed go before its effect: approval-gate consume ... | complete <request-id> <outcome>.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman approval-gate consume <go-file> <action> <target> <revision> <draft-file|->
       herdsman approval-gate complete <request-id> <outcome>

Binds a relayed go to one effect: consume checks the go and records the
request (CONSUME, DUPLICATE, RECONCILE or REFUSED lines); complete records
its outcome (COMPLETED). --json prints each line as an Event object.

settings: HERDSMAN_INBOX (the inbox folder) is required. HERDSMAN_PREFLIGHT
names the setup proof, <inbox>/setup.json, which must name this herdsman
binary with its checksum. HEALTH_AFTER (1 to 86400) and LOCK_WAIT (1 to 60) are
strict settings. Herdr is reached through HERDR_SOCKET_PATH.

exit codes:
  0  consumed or completed; act once
  1  refused: the go does not bind this effect
  2  usage error, HERDSMAN_INBOX is not set, an invalid setting, or the
     inbox cannot be used
  3  a human must repeat the setup: the proof is missing, stale, or does
     not name this herdsman binary (an old proof that lists scripts too)
  4  a duplicate: the request already has an outcome
  5  reconcile: consumed without an outcome; inspect external state first

exitCodes.meaning: consumed or completed; act once
refused: the go does not bind this effect
usage error, HERDSMAN_INBOX is not set, an invalid setting, or the inbox cannot be used
a human must repeat the setup: the proof is missing, stale, or does not name this herdsman binary (an old proof that lists scripts too)
a duplicate: the request already has an outcome
reconcile: consumed without an outcome; inspect external state first

commands.name: commit
commands.summary: Commit a worktree with a Conventional Commits message.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman commit [--squash <target>] [--dry-run] [-m <message>] [--type <type>] [--scope <scope>] [--json]

Stages the current worktree by its [commit] stage policy and commits. The
message is written by the configured generator, from the staged diff, and must
be a Conventional Commits message. When no generator can answer, the command
writes a plain one from the branch and the file names and says so; an answer
that is still invalid after one retry stops the commit.

--squash folds every commit since the branch left <target> into this one.
--dry-run shows the request, which program gets it and its answer; nothing changes.

exit codes:
  0  committed, or the dry run printed
  1  nothing to commit, an invalid message, or git refused
  2  bad usage

exitCodes.meaning: committed, or the dry run printed
nothing to commit, an invalid message, or git refused
bad usage

commands.name: each
commands.summary: Run a command in every worktree.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman each [--json] -- <command> [<arg>...]

Runs a command in each worktree of the repository in turn; a failure in one
does not stop the rest. The command is run as given, without a shell; use
sh -c '...' for one. It sees HERDSMAN_TASK, HERDSMAN_BRANCH and
HERDSMAN_WORKTREE_PATH, and reads nothing from standard input.

The command's output goes to standard output. The heading before each run and
the summary go to standard error, so the output can be piped. With --json the
command's output moves to standard error too and standard output holds only the
results.

exit codes:
  0  the command succeeded everywhere
  1  it failed somewhere, or the worktrees could not be listed
  2  bad usage

exitCodes.meaning: the command succeeded everywhere
it failed somewhere, or the worktrees could not be listed
bad usage

commands.name: run-check
commands.summary: Run one heavy check at a time on this machine, behind a load gate (--publish <hours>: the load reading).
commands.help:
usage: herdsman run-check <command> [args]
       herdsman run-check --publish <hours>

Runs one heavy check at a time on this machine, under a shared lock, behind
a load gate, at a lower priority. --publish writes the machine's load
reading every HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_EVERY for <hours> (or
HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_SECONDS), at most a day.

settings: HERDSMAN_LOCK, HERDSMAN_READING, HERDSMAN_LOCK_WAIT (5400),
HERDSMAN_GATE_WAIT (600), HERDSMAN_GATE_POLL (15), HERDSMAN_MIN_FREE (10),
HERDSMAN_NICE (10), HERDSMAN_LOAD_LIMIT (the core count), HERDSMAN_PROBES,
HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_EVERY (15), HERDSMAN_PUBLISH_SECONDS. Durations are seconds
or a number with s, m, h or d.

exit codes:
  N   the check's own exit code
  2   an invalid setting or hour count; nothing ran
  64  usage error
  69  the lock file cannot be opened or locked
  70  the start marker cannot be written
  73  the publisher cannot write its reading (--publish)
  75  the load gate gave up, or no lock came within HERDSMAN_LOCK_WAIT
  126 the command cannot be started
  127 the command was not found

exitCodes.meaning: the check's own exit code
an invalid setting or hour count; nothing ran
usage error
the lock file cannot be opened or locked
the start marker cannot be written
the publisher cannot write its reading (--publish)
the load gate gave up, or no lock came within HERDSMAN_LOCK_WAIT
the command cannot be started
the command was not found

commands.name: wait
commands.summary: Wait for the next event of the loop (a report, a review, a blocked or stalled agent, a health flag), or TICK.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman wait

Polls every POLL (60) and returns after the first pass with events
(REPORT, REPORT-UPDATED, REVIEW, BLOCKED, GOAL-DONE-NO-REPORT, STALL,
OVERDUE, HEALTH), or after DEADLINE (1500) with a TICK line.
HERDSMAN_HEALTH_EVERY (300) paces the health check; HERDSMAN_DUE_<name> is
a due time in Unix seconds. Durations are seconds or a number with s, m, h
or d, at most a day.

exit codes:
  0  events or a TICK were printed
  2  usage error, or an invalid setting; nothing ran

exitCodes.meaning: events or a TICK were printed
usage error, or an invalid setting; nothing ran

commands.name: watch
commands.summary: Watch implementers, the reviewer or pull requests: herdsman watch implementers|reviewer|prs.
commands.help:
usage: herdsman watch implementers|reviewer|prs

implementers and reviewer print events until interrupted; prs returns on
the first pull request change, or after HERDSMAN_PR_DEADLINE (1500) with a
TICK line, polling every HERDSMAN_PR_INTERVAL (120).

exit codes:
  0  a change or a TICK was printed, or the watcher was stopped
  1  no gh token, or a pull request could not be read three polls in a
     row
  2  usage error, or a missing or invalid setting; nothing ran

exitCodes.meaning: a change or a TICK was printed, or the watcher was stopped
no gh token, or a pull request could not be read three polls in a row
usage error, or a missing or invalid setting; nothing ran
